title: This Is Marketing
author: Seth Godin
blurb: Seth Godin argues that marketing is not about advertising, hype, or tricking people into buying. It is the generous work of helping people solve a problem and become who they hope to become. Instead of chasing everyone, he urges you to choose a smallest viable market: a specific group whose worldview you understand and whose needs you can serve better than anyone else. From there, you position your work on the edges others ignore, tell stories that match what your audience already believes, and create the tension that makes change feel worth it. Godin shows how status, belonging, and the idea that people like us do things like this drive almost every decision. The goal is to earn permission and trust over time, so the people you serve come to depend on you and spread the word for you.

lessons.t: Marketing Is the Act of Making Change
lessons.b: Marketing is not shouting or manipulating but the generous work of helping people become who they want to become.

lessons.b: Instead of trying to reach everyone, choose the smallest group you can truly delight and serve them so well they can't imagine life without you.
